name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We should adopt a single 4px #005fcc focus ring with a 2px white box-shadow blur on every interactive element. This decision provides a clear visual indicator of focus for keyboard users while being subtle enough not to overwhelm sighted users. By choosing a single focus ring, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially less visual distinction between different types of interactive elements, but gaining consistency and simplicity in our design. This approach also aligns with our goal of making EXCAVA usable by everyone, as it provides a clear and consistent way for users to navigate the site using their keyboard.

name: Reader
text: The single 4px ring fails on high-contrast modes—it disappears against white backgrounds. A double ring (4px #005fcc + 2px white inset) keeps visibility in all modes but risks clutter on dense interfaces. Test both in Windows High Contrast Mode and on a crowded mobile screen; the artifact is the test report.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt the double ring: 4px #005fcc solid ring with a 2px solid white inner ring. This keeps focus visible in Windows High Contrast Mode and against any background, meeting our "usable by everyone" rule. The trade-off is a slightly heavier visual weight on dense screens, but sighted users can still scan quickly, and the clarity for assistive tech users outweighs the clutter risk.

name: Reader
text: The double ring still risks visual clutter on small or dense interfaces—especially for users with low vision who rely on magnification. A better alternative is a single 3px #005fcc ring with a 1px white inset, tested in both high-contrast and mobile views. Settle it by running a Playwright MCP test comparing task completion time and error rates for keyboard users in both modes.
